spec: Given a string s, return a dictionary mapping each distinct character that appears in s to a list of every index (in ascending order) at which it occurs. An empty string returns an empty dictionary.
Given a string s, count the number of maximal runs of consecutive digit characters in s (any non-digit character ends the current run and does not itself count). A string with no digits returns 0.

Given two strings a and b, return True if there is a one-to-one character mapping from a to b such that replacing every occurrence of each character in a with its mapped character produces b exactly, and the mapping is consistent in both directions. Strings of different lengths are never isomorphic and return False.

Given a string s, return True if s is non-empty and its first character is identical to its last character (a single-character string always satisfies this since it is its own first and last character). Return False for an empty string.

Given a string s, count the number of maximal contiguous groups of characters that share the same class, where the three classes are letters, digits, and everything else (such as punctuation or spaces). An empty string returns 0.
Given a string s, return the concatenation of s with its own reverse appended immediately after it (s followed by s reversed). An empty string returns an empty string.
Given a string s, return the index of the first uppercase letter found in s, scanning left to right. Return -1 if s contains no uppercase letters, including for an empty string.

Given a string s, return a copy with characters swapped in adjacent pairs: the character at index 0 swaps with the character at index 1, index 2 swaps with index 3, and so on. If s has odd length, the final unpaired character stays in its original place.

Given a list of strings, return the longest common prefix shared by all of them when compared case-insensitively, but return the prefix using the exact original casing found in the first string of the list. An empty list returns an empty string.

Given a string s, return a copy of s where every vowel letter (a, e, i, o, u, either case) is replaced by an underscore character, while every non-vowel character, including its original case, stays exactly in place.
Return the input string with its characters in reverse order. Handle the empty string by returning the empty string. Works for any string, including strings with spaces, digits, and punctuation.

Split the string on whitespace into words and return a new string where each word has its first character uppercased and every remaining character lowercased, with the resulting words joined by single spaces. An empty string, or a string with only whitespace, returns an empty string.

Determine whether two strings are anagrams of each other, ignoring case and ignoring spaces but treating all other characters (including punctuation and digits) as significant. Return True if, after lowercasing and removing spaces, the two strings contain exactly the same characters the same number of times, and False otherwise.

Return a new string where every uppercase letter is converted to lowercase and every lowercase letter is converted to uppercase. Characters that are not letters (digits, punctuation, spaces) are left unchanged in their original position.

Validate a string that must contain only the characters '(' and ')'. Return True if the parentheses are balanced (every '(' has a matching later ')', never more closes than opens at any point, and counts are equal overall) and no other character appears; otherwise return False.

Validate a string that must contain only the characters '[' and ']'. Return True if the square brackets are balanced (properly nested, equal counts, never more closes than opens at any point) and no other character appears; otherwise return False.

Validate a string that may contain letters, digits and the bracket characters '()[]{}' mixed freely. Ignore all non-bracket characters, and return True if the bracket characters that remain (in order) are properly matched and nested by type, otherwise return False.

Validate a string that may contain only the characters '(', ')', '[' and ']' (no curly braces). Return True if the brackets are properly nested and matched by type in the correct order, otherwise return False. An empty string is valid.

Validate a string that may contain '(', ')' and backslash-escaped versions '\\(' and '\\)' (a backslash followed by a parenthesis is a literal character, not a bracket, and consumes two characters). Return True if the remaining unescaped parentheses are balanced, otherwise return False. Any other character is allowed and ignored.

Validate a string containing round brackets '(' ')' and single-quoted substrings delimited by the character "'" (quotes always appear in properly closed, non-nested pairs). Ignore any parenthesis that occurs strictly inside a quoted substring. Return True if the parentheses outside of quotes are balanced, otherwise return False.

Given two lists of distinct integers, `pushed` and `popped` of the same length, determine whether `popped` could be the result of a valid sequence of stack push and pop operations where the elements are pushed in the exact order given by `pushed`, interleaved with pops that must always pop the current top of the stack, ending with an empty stack. Return True if such an interleaving exists, otherwise False.

Determine whether a string containing '(', ')' and '*' can be turned into a validly balanced parenthesis string, where each '*' may be treated as '(', as ')', or as an empty string. Return True if at least one such interpretation makes the parentheses balanced, otherwise return False.

Validate a string of simplified HTML-like tags, where every tag is either an opening tag '<x>' or a closing tag '</x>' with x a single lowercase letter (no attributes). Return True if every opening tag has a matching closing tag with the same letter, properly nested in the correct order, and there is no leftover text between tags; otherwise return False.

Validate a string of digit characters using the Luhn algorithm (used to check credit-card-like numbers). Starting from the rightmost digit and moving left, double every second digit; if doubling produces a number greater than 9, subtract 9 from it. Sum all the resulting digits (doubled and untouched). Return True if the total is divisible by 10 and the string has at least 2 digit characters and contains only digits, otherwise return False.

Validate a credit-card-style string of the format 'XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX' where each X is a digit: exactly four groups of four digits separated by hyphens. Additionally the 16 digits (read without hyphens) must pass the Luhn checksum (double every second digit from the right, subtracting 9 if over 9, and the total must be divisible by 10). Return True only if both the format and the checksum are valid.

Validate a credit-card-style string of the format 'XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX' where each X is a digit: exactly four groups of four digits separated by single spaces. Additionally the 16 digits (read without spaces) must pass the Luhn checksum (double every second digit from the right, subtracting 9 if over 9, and the total must be divisible by 10). Return True only if both the format and the checksum are valid.

Validate a UPC-A barcode: a string of exactly 12 digit characters. Compute the check digit as follows: sum the digits in odd positions (1st, 3rd, ..., 11th, 1-indexed) and multiply by 3, add the sum of digits in even positions (2nd, 4th, ..., 12th); the total must be divisible by 10 for the code to be valid. Return False if the string is not exactly 12 digits.

Validate an ISBN-10 string. The input may contain hyphens, which should be removed first. After removing hyphens, the result must be exactly 10 characters: the first 9 must be digits, and the 10th must be a digit or the uppercase letter 'X' (representing the value 10). Compute the checksum as the sum of each character's value multiplied by its weight (10 down to 1, left to right); the ISBN is valid if this sum is divisible by 11.

Validate an ISBN-13 string. The input may contain hyphens, which should be removed first. After removing hyphens, the result must be exactly 13 digit characters. Compute the checksum by multiplying each digit by an alternating weight starting with 1 for the first digit, then 3, then 1, then 3, and so on; the ISBN is valid if the total sum is divisible by 10.

Validate a US bank routing number (ABA number): a string of exactly 9 digit characters d1..d9. Compute checksum = 3*(d1+d4+d7) + 7*(d2+d5+d8) + 1*(d3+d6+d9). Return True if the string is exactly 9 digits and this checksum is divisible by 10, otherwise return False.

Validate an EAN-8 barcode: a string of exactly 8 digit characters d1..d8, where d8 is the check digit. Multiply d1,d3,d5,d7 by 3 and d2,d4,d6 by 1, sum the results, and compute check = (10 - (sum % 10)) % 10. Return True if this equals d8 and the string is exactly 8 digits, otherwise return False.

Validate a serial-number checksum: a string of exactly 8 uppercase alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9). Treat the first 7 characters as the payload and the 8th as the check character, which must be a digit. Compute the sum of the payload characters' positions in the sequence '0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ' (0-indexed), take that sum modulo 10, and compare it (as a string digit) to the 8th character. Return True if they match and the format is correct, otherwise False.

Validate a simple email address string. It must contain exactly one '@' splitting it into a local part and a domain part. The local part must be non-empty, contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens or plus signs, and must not start or end with a dot or contain two consecutive dots. The domain part must split by dots into at least two labels, each non-empty and containing only letters, digits or internal hyphens (not leading/trailing), and the final label (the TLD) must be purely alphabetic with length at least 2.

Validate a hashtag string. It must start with '#' followed by 1 to 30 characters, the first of which must be an alphabetic letter, and all of which must be letters, digits, or underscores (no spaces or punctuation). Return False otherwise.

Validate a mention string used to tag another user. It must start with '@' followed by a username: 3 to 16 characters, the first an alphabetic letter, the rest letters, digits, or underscores. Return False otherwise.

Validate a simple URL string. It must start with 'http://' or 'https://', contain no spaces anywhere, and be followed by a non-empty domain made of dot-separated labels (each label non-empty, alphanumeric with optional internal hyphens not at the start/end) with at least two labels and a purely alphabetic final label (TLD) of length at least 2. An optional path beginning with '/' may follow the domain with no further validation on the path other than containing no spaces.
Validate a URL slug string: it must consist only of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, must not start or end with a hyphen, must not contain two consecutive hyphens, and must be non-empty.

Validate a file name against a list of allowed lowercase extensions (given as the second argument). The file name must contain exactly one dot separating a non-empty base name from an extension; the base name may contain only letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens; and the extension must appear (case-sensitively, already lowercase) in the allowed extensions list.

Validate a business email address. It must contain exactly one '@' splitting it into a local part and domain part. The local part must be non-empty, contain only letters, digits, dots, hyphens, or plus signs (no underscores), and must not start/end with a dot or contain consecutive dots. The domain must split into at least two dot-separated labels, each non-empty with only letters, digits and internal hyphens, and the final label must be exactly one of 'com', 'org', 'net', or 'io'.

Validate a URL query string. It must start with '?' and be followed by one or more 'key=value' pairs joined by '&'. Each key and value must be non-empty and consist only of alphanumeric characters, and each pair must contain exactly one '=' sign. Return False if the format is violated in any way.
